findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the agentic degrade record a failure class for every non-clean run the parent lists (limit exhaustion, invalid output, truncation, refusal, provider error, timeout), not only for errors that already carry `.outcome`, and add one test per class.
evidence: Parent invariant (epic 9794-4336-5ed6-4561, Fail closed): 'An agentic run that does not finish cleanly ... tool-step or iteration limit exhausted, a truncated (max_tokens) or refused ... response, or output that fails validation — resolves INDETERMINATE through the same resolution_class path a failed pipeline pass uses, records `engine` and the failure class on coverage'.

Leaf: 'records the failure class (`resolution_class`, `disposition`) through the existing `failure.outcome_of` path whenever the raised error carries an outcome ... an error without one degrades with no class, as today.'

Code: run_failure.interpret_failure raises LLMBudgetExhaustedError for UsageLimitExceeded with only `.diagnostic` set, not `.outcome` (src/rebar/llm/run_failure.py:77-83). Existing LLMError subclasses (StructuredOutputError for invalid output, RunawayToolLoopError) are re-raised with a diagnostic but no outcome (run_failure.py:84-112). Only the generic provider arm attaches `.outcome` (run_failure.py:139-149). failure.outcome_of returns None when no `.outcome` is attached (failure.py:580-584).

The leaf's Testing covers only `LLMUnavailableError` with an outcome and a plain `RuntimeError` with no class. No test covers limit exhaustion, invalid output, truncation or refusal recording a class.
No sibling covers it: foliated-oceangoing-parrot handles only the attestation engine field. The other siblings handle surfaces, the comparison harness, production checks and the sunset.
findings.finding: The leaf narrows the parent's Fail-closed invariant: a failure class is recorded only when the raised error already carries `.outcome`. Limit exhaustion and schema-invalid output, both named by the parent, raise errors with no outcome, so they would degrade with no failure class. The parent requires engine AND failure class on coverage for every non-clean agentic run (divergent_implementation: omits_required_site).
findings.location: Approach → 'Failed and degraded runs' (first bullet); Testing → 'Failure'
scenarios: The agent hits its 80-request budget → LLMBudgetExhaustedError (no `.outcome`) → INDETERMINATE with coverage.engine='agentic' but no resolution_class, which falls short of the parent invariant.
The agent's structured output fails validation → StructuredOutputError re-raised without `.outcome` → INDETERMINATE with no failure class.
findings.suggested_fix: Under engine == "agentic", when failure.outcome_of(last_error) is None, classify the exception with failure.classify_llm_failure(exc, ClassifyContext(model=<frontier id>)), which is documented as never raising, and record that class. Add Testing cases that raise LLMBudgetExhaustedError and StructuredOutputError and assert a non-empty resolution_class plus coverage.engine == "agentic" with zero attestations. findings.finding: The plan says the three shortcuts (idempotent_reuse, verdict_reuse, drift_refresh) are the ways a pipeline run can consume an agentic run's state, and it adds an engine guard only to those three. Other pipeline-only consumers also read the latest REVIEW_RESULT sidecar without checking its engine. A later pipeline review would treat an agentic sidecar as its prior: `_maybe_apply_rising_floor` scores advisory novelty against `sidecar.surfaced_findings(latest_review_result)` and drops findings; `sidecar.prior_concerns` feeds prior findings with priority ≥ 0.5 into Pass-1 recall, and an agentic `major` gets 0.7; `remediation_mode` uses the latest sidecar as its eligibility baseline; `drift_floor` reads `latest_review_result`. Once agentic sidecars carry real block/advisory findings, these paths judge a pipeline review against agentic findings.

findings.finding: `reuse.latest_review_engine` reads the latest sidecar's coverage.engine and uses it as the engine that earned the current attestation. The two can disagree, so the guard can still let a pipeline run replay or re-sign an agentic PASS, which is the exact failure the section exists to prevent. claim_gate_check, the reuse authority for idempotent_reuse, never looks at the sidecar. scenarios: An agentic PASS signs attestation A. A pipeline review of the unchanged plan sees basis=agentic, runs in full and ends BLOCK, emitting a sidecar with no engine key. findings.finding: The plan reads the engine from the latest sidecar and treats an absent value as `"pipeline"`. That only works if every signed agentic PASS is followed by a sidecar naming it, and the code does not guarantee this. In `_run_plan_review`, `sidecar.emit` runs only `if emit_sidecar`, and the code comment calls it best-effort. So an agentic PASS can be signed with no sidecar written, or the emit can fail. Separately, a later pipeline run (for example a degraded INDETERMINATE) can write a newer sidecar while the agentic attestation stays valid. In each case `latest_review_engine` returns `"pipeline"` for a ticket whose attestation was signed by the agent. The pipeline's `idempotent_reuse` or `drift_refresh` would then reuse or re-sign that agentic PASS, which is exactly what the guard was added to prevent.
findings.location: Approach → Reuse shortcuts stay engine-matched (`reuse.latest_review_engine`)
scenarios: `review_plan(engine="agentic", emit_sidecar=False)` signs a PASS, then `review_plan(engine="pipeline")` finds no sidecar, takes `basis == "pipeline"`, and `idempotent_reuse` returns the agentic attestation as a pipeline reuse.
An agentic PASS is signed and then a pipeline run degrades to INDETERMINATE, so the newest sidecar has no `engine`. The next pipeline run's `drift_refresh` re-signs the agentic attestation.
findings.suggested_fix: Match the sidecar to the attestation before trusting its engine. Only use a sidecar whose `material_fingerprint`/`reviewed_at` matches the current signed attestation; otherwise return a value other than `"pipeline"` (for example `"unknown"`) so all three shortcuts stay off. Alternatively, when engine == "agentic", always emit the sidecar after signing (or do not sign if the emit fails).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Either give a positive reason for disabling reuse under agentic, or switch idempotent_reuse/verdict_reuse to a `basis == engine` guard (drift_refresh stays pipeline-only) and add agentic-reuse tests.

findings.finding: Under `engine == "agentic"` the plan turns off every reuse shortcut ('every agentic review runs the agent') and gives no reason. A structurally simpler option keeps reuse per engine: guard idempotent_reuse and verdict_reuse on `basis == engine` instead of `engine == "pipeline" and basis == "pipeline"`. Both are engine-neutral: one replays a valid attestation, the other a fingerprint-matched BLOCK sidecar. Only drift_refresh, whose probe re-runs pipeline criteria, would stay pipeline-only. As planned, re-reviewing an unchanged plan always costs a frontier agent run (budget up to 80 requests), and the BLOCK-loop protection from 7e77 is lost for agentic. A resampled BLOCK after a signed agentic PASS also leaves the latest sidecar saying BLOCK while the attestation still certifies the plan.
findings.location: Approach › Reuse shortcuts stay engine-matched ("Under \"agentic\" the shortcuts stay off")
scenarios: An agent loop or a user re-runs review-plan on an unchanged, agentic-certified plan. Each run pays for a full frontier agent, and a nondeterministic BLOCK replaces the PASS as the latest sidecar while the attestation stays valid.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the first two guards with `engine == basis and ...` (basis read once). Keep `engine == "pipeline" and basis == "pipeline"` only for drift_refresh. Add tests: an agentic signed PASS followed by an agentic review reports idempotent_skip; an agentic BLOCK followed by an agentic review reports verdict_reuse.

If the change is reverted, the old reuse guards check only `engine == "pipeline"` and never `basis`. A pipeline run on an unchanged ticket would then replay the agentic BLOCK through `verdict_reuse`, or reuse/re-sign the agentic PASS through `idempotent_reuse`/`drift_refresh`, without telling the caller. The plan does not say how the post-rollback state should look, or whether operators must force a re-review of tickets the agent reviewed.

findings.finding: The plan engine-matches only the three reuse shortcuts. Other pipeline paths read `sidecar.latest_review_result` too and will treat an agentic sidecar as the pipeline's own prior review: the rising/novelty floor's prior set, Pass-1 `prior_concerns` recall, the remediation-mode eligibility baselines and the drift-floor decision.
